resolutions.researcher_notes: Recovered the origin akhbarlibya24.net piece (2020-05-10; verified 200 OK, contains 'بوصة'). Full text (via translation) says: Mellitah Oil & Gas's Operations Dept. was building a 4-inch BACKUP gas line from the main production station to the GT11/GT12 power-generation units at Abu Attifel field, needed because those units currently depend solely on the NGL plant; as of the article the work was ~60% complete, expected done by end of May 2020. Nothing in this source says the project was cancelled -- it reads as an active, nearly-finished project. Searched further (English + Arabic: Libya Herald/Observer, attaqa, eanlibya, NOC.ly, Mellitah OG site, Oil Review Africa/Petroleum Africa Abu Attifel coverage) for any later update (completion notice, abandonment, incident) -- found none either way; Abu Attifel field itself has continued normal maintenance/restart cycles through 2020-2024 with no reported disruption tied to this specific backup line. Cannot source Status=cancelled from any independent reporting. Separately: GEM's own wiki page for this same PID (read for leads only, not cited) currently carries Status='Under construction', not cancelled -- i.e. the tracker's own reference material disagrees internally with the sheet's cancelled value, another sign 'cancelled' has no support. No ShelvedCancelledType is recorded either, consistent with the value never having been substantiated. Recommend: revert Status question to the researcher/human reviewer -- evidence points away from cancelled, not toward it.

The article's own title/text is explicitly 'خط الغاز' (gas line); it is a natural-gas backup feed line, supporting Fuel=Gas. Single strong primary source (the announcement itself); no second independent outlet covered this local project, so tier=medium, independent=false.
Dated 2020-05-10, describing the line as under active construction (~60% complete, expected finished by end of that month) -- supports ConstructionYear=2020. Single source, tier=medium.
Text explicitly states 'خط احتياطي بقطر 4 بوصة' (a backup line of 4-inch diameter) -- directly supports Diameter=4/in. Single source, tier=medium.

The recorded StartLocation/EndLocation (Mellitah Port -> Bu-Attifel oil field, ~900-1000 km apart) are NOT supported by the source and are almost certainly a mis-parse of the headline. 'مليتة' in the title is Mellitah Oil & Gas COMPANY (the operator, a joint venture of NOC/Eni), not the geographic Mellitah industrial complex/port. The article describes the line as running entirely WITHIN the Abu Attifel field: from the field's main production station to the on-site GT11/GT12 electricity-generation units, as a backup supply route for when the field's own NGL plant is down for maintenance. There is no route to or from the Mellitah coastal complex at all. See __VALIDITY__ for full discussion; recommend both Start/EndLocation be corrected to reflect a short intra-field line at Abu Attifel, not a Mellitah-to-Sirte-Basin transmission route.

(a) Endpoints: CONFIRMED WRONG. The origin akhbarlibya24.net article (2020-05-10, verified) is about a short 4-inch BACKUP gas line built entirely inside the Abu Attifel oil field/Sirte Basin -- from the field's main production station to its own GT11/GT12 power-generation units -- so those units are not solely dependent on the field's NGL plant during its maintenance outages. 'Mellitah' in the headline/row is the operating company (Mellitah Oil & Gas Co., the NOC/Eni JV that operates Abu Attifel), not the geographic Mellitah coastal complex/port ~900-1000 km away. No source supports any pipe running between the two places, and a 4-inch line over that distance would be physically implausible as a transmission trunk, consistent with the brief's expectation. This row's endpoints (StartLocation=Mellitah/Mellitah Port, EndLocation=Bu-Attifel oil field/Sirte Basin) should both be corrected to a single-site location: Abu Attifel field, Sirte Basin, Libya (both start and end within the field). (b) Cancellation: NOT SOURCED. Found no report, in Arabic or English (checked Libya Herald, Libya Observer, Al Wasat, attaqa, eanlibya, NOC.ly, Mellitah OG's own site, Oil Review Africa/Petroleum Africa Abu Attifel coverage 2020-2024), stating this backup line was cancelled, abandoned, or completed. The only source (the 2020-05-10 announcement) describes it as ~60% built and due to finish within weeks -- i.e. near-completion, not a project being scrapped. 'No update since 2020' (the existing researcher note) is silence, not evidence of cancellation, per protocol. GEM's own wiki entry for this PID (read for leads only) in fact currently shows Status='Under construction', contradicting the sheet's 'cancelled' -- suggesting the cancelled status was never substantiated and may be an error/placeholder. Flagging separately per the brief: Status=cancelled also carries NO ShelvedCancelledType, which is itself a data-completeness gap regardless of the status verdict. Scope note for the human reviewer (not my call): if the endpoints are corrected as in (a), this becomes a ~short, likely well-under-1km, 4-inch site utility/backup feeder entirely within one field -- exactly the class of intra-facility service line GGIT's inclusion threshold is generally meant to exclude; worth a explicit in/out-of-scope decision rather than just a location fix.
